implementation_notes: The framework implements the roles: AbstractMessageSplitter.splitMessage(Message<?>) returns a Collection, an Iterator, a Stream or even a Flux, and the endpoint fills CORRELATION_ID, SEQUENCE_NUMBER and SEQUENCE_SIZE on every derived message so a downstream aggregator can recombine them. Return an Iterator/Iterable (rather than a materialised collection) to split without holding all parts in memory - SEQUENCE_SIZE is then 0, so the default SequenceSizeReleaseStrategy cannot complete a group and a custom ReleaseStrategy or group timeout is required. A plain POJO method taking one argument and returning a collection works as well and is easier to unit-test than subclassing the splitter.
pitfalls: An Iterator/Iterable result leaves SEQUENCE_SIZE at 0, so the default aggregator release strategy never completes the group; configure a custom ReleaseStrategy or send-partial-result-on-expiry.
Returning null ends the flow without splitting, and an empty collection is only reported if a discardChannel is configured - silent drops are easy to miss.
The splitter must only split: per-part enrichment belongs in a following transformer, otherwise a route change forces a rewrite of the splitter.
Reusing one handler bean across several <splitter> definitions with injected output channels is rejected at configuration time; use prototype scope or a dedicated bean.

variants.name: In-process Stream pipeline (flatMap / mapMulti)
variants.implementation_notes: Inside the JVM the splitter is a stream operator: flatMap replaces each composite element with the stream of its parts, and mapMulti (Java 16+) emits several parts from one element without allocating an intermediate Stream, so one pipeline expresses split-then-send. This is the right form when the composite is already an in-memory collection and no messaging topology is involved; a Stream is lazy and single-use, so only the terminal operation publishes and the pipeline cannot be replayed.
pitfalls: A Stream is consumed once: reusing a stored stream (or a 'forked' one) throws IllegalStateException.
flatMap's mapper must be stateless and non-interfering; a counter mutated in the lambda is a data race under parallel(), and forEach in a parallel stream does not preserve encounter order.
Close resource-backed streams (Files.lines) with try-with-resources or the file descriptor leaks after the split.

variants.name: Apache Camel split() EIP in a route DSL
variants.implementation_notes: Camel exposes the pattern as a route node: split(expression) evaluates an expression - body, tokenize, XPath, JSONPath - into an Iterator, Iterable, array, Collection, Map, NodeList or delimited String and routes one exchange per element, with the exchange properties CamelSplitIndex / CamelSplitSize / CamelSplitComplete carrying correlation and completion. streaming splits on demand instead of materialising all parts, parallelProcessing adds a thread pool, group batches N parts into one message, and stopOnException / errorThreshold / maxFailedRecords decide what a failed part means. Camel 4 requires Java 17, so this form has a higher floor than the Spring Integration one.
pitfalls: Without streaming=true the whole composite is materialised into exchanges before the first part is processed.
A String body is split on commas by default - a route that forgets tokenize/delimiter silently splits on commas.
parallelProcessing with an AggregationStrategy requires a thread-safe strategy, otherwise results interleave; error thresholds also become non-deterministic under parallelism.
Resume/watermark support requires a configured watermark store; without it a restart replays the whole composite instead of resuming at the last completed part.
